record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Measure and determine the quark transversity distribution δq(x,Q²) in the nucleon. The leading-twist quark spin distributions in a nucleon include the unpolarized distribution q(x,Q²), the helicity distribution Δq(x,Q²), and the transversity distribution δq(x,Q²); δq governs helicity-flip or transverse-polarization physics and can be interpreted as the probability of finding quarks with momentum fraction x transversely polarized in a transversely polarized nucleon at infinite momentum. The open question is what δq(x,Q²) is experimentally and how to access it through processes such as transversely polarized Drell-Yan or semi-inclusive DIS with helicity-flip fragmentation.

evidence.quote: We now know that the transversity, δq(x, Q2), together with the unpolarized distribution, q(x, Q2), and the helicity distribution, Δq(x, Q2), are required to give a complete description of the quark spin in the nucleon at leading twist.
In contrast nothing is known about transversity from experiment, because it decouples from inclusive DIS on account of a selection rule.
Measurements of quark transversity rank high on the agendas of Hermes, COMPASS and RHIC.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
At leading twist, the spin structure of a quark of flavor q inside a nucleon at momentum fraction x and resolution scale Q² is described by three collinear parton distribution functions: the unpolarized distribution q(x,Q²), the longitudinal helicity distribution Δq(x,Q²), and the transversity distribution δq(x,Q²). The transversity δq(x,Q²) admits the probabilistic interpretation, in the infinite-momentum frame, of the number density of quarks of flavor q with momentum fraction x whose transverse polarization is aligned with the transverse polarization of the nucleon, minus the number density of those with opposite transverse polarization. Because δq is chiral-odd, it decouples from fully inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and must be accessed in processes containing a second chiral-odd object, e.g. transversely polarized Drell–Yan production, or semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering with a chiral-odd fragmentation function (Collins fragmentation, dihadron interference fragmentation, etc.).

Problem: Determine the transversity distributions δq(x,Q²) for the light quark flavors (q = u, d, and where possible s and antiquarks) in the nucleon as functions of x at a reference scale Q². Specifically, extract δq(x,Q²) from experimental data on suitable hard processes (transversely polarized Drell–Yan, semi-inclusive DIS with helicity-flip fragmentation, dihadron production, etc.), including their x-dependence, flavor dependence, integrated tensor charges δq = ∫₀¹[δq(x) − δq̄(x)]dx, and the associated uncertainties.
artifact.status_search_result: Since this question was posed, several global QCD analyses (e.g. Kang–Prokudin–Sun–Yuan 2015 and subsequent JAM/MAP collaboration fits) have extracted u- and d-quark transversity using Collins-asymmetry SIDIS data from HERMES/COMPASS/Belle and dihadron interference data. Lattice QCD calculations (2024) have also computed isovector and isoscalar transversity PDFs and tensor charges. However, transversity is still significantly less constrained than the unpolarized and helicity distributions, especially for sea quarks and at small/large x; transversely polarized Drell–Yan measurements (RHIC, COMPASS) are ongoing. The problem is therefore partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Extraction of Quark Transversity Distribution and Collins Fragmentation Functions with QCD Evolution
status_evidence.snippet: Global extraction of u and d quark transversity distributions with QCD evolution from SIDIS and e+e- data.
status_evidence.claim: Phenomenological extractions of light-quark transversity now exist.

status_evidence.title: Transversity PDFs of the proton from lattice QCD with physical quark masses
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice QCD calculation of isovector and isoscalar transversity PDFs and tensor charges at NLO matching.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice QCD provides first-principles determinations of transversity, complementing experimental extractions.
